items.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: And we used to listen to big bands, Fletcher Henderson, Earl Hines, Basie when he first went to New York, and all the big bands you know, Jimmie Lunceford.

ctx.x: Did your parents have blues recordings, or where did you hear most of your music?

At the player piano. And we had some blues on that. And then we got a radio. And we used to listen to big bands, Fletcher Henderson, Earl Hines, Basie when he first went to New York, and all the big bands you know, Jimmie Lunceford.
Radio was a huge part of the way information was spread at the time, right?

items.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Basically stuff like Basie, Jimmy Lunceford, Benny Goodman, John Coltrane, you know people like that. It’s background.

ctx.x: Do you hear new stuff that you like, that perks your ear up.
Every now and then. Basically stuff like Basie, Jimmy Lunceford, Benny Goodman, John Coltrane, you know people like that. It’s background. Until I turn on the T.V. and I turn it off.
